messages:
Alice Chen: hitting a hang in python SDK streaming again — generator stops yielding after a fragmented heartbeat + partial token. Repro script attached below. Happens on 0.9.3 and 0.9.4.

Ben Patel: can you paste minimal repro + logs? is this on hosted or dedicated? any auth rotation happening?

Alice Chen: hosted API, token stable for the session. Repro is a simple SSE loop using sdk.StreamingClient.stream(). It yields for a few tokens then stalls forever, no exception. We see keepalive heartbeats every 15s.

Carla Gomes: saw something similar earlier — the parser expects a blank line delimiter and drops state if chunk boundary splits "\n\n" across frames. Might be a split between token bytes and heartbeat.

Alice Chen: adding logs. snippet of receive stream bytes: 
```\nchunk1: b'data: {"delta":"Hel'\nchunk2: b'lo"}\r\n\r\n\nkeepalive: \n'\nchunk3: b'data: [DONE]\r\n\r\n'\n```\nAfter chunk2 the SDK's generator never yields, even though chunk3 contains [DONE].

Ben Patel: thanks. can you try forcing the SSE parser to be tolerant? quick workaround: upgrade to 0.9.6 or set client.stream_parser_mode = "lenient" (temporary). Also try setting socket read timeout shorter so underlying loop notices activity.

Alice Chen: tried lenient parser — it resumed and produced [DONE], but crashed later with a unicode decode error on multibyte split. log: `UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode bytes in position 2-3: unexpected end of data`

Carla Gomes: ok that points to multi-byte char split across recv. parser should accumulate bytes and decode only on full sequences. Looks like current code decodes per-chunk. repro snippet: 
```\nfrom redwood import StreamingClient\nc = StreamingClient(api_key=ENV['REDWOOD_KEY'])\nwith c.stream(model='rwd-3b', input='hello', stream=True) as gen:\n    for event in gen:\n        print(event)\n```\n
Ben Patel: next steps I need from you: 1) full tcpdump of one failing session (pcap), 2) exact sdk wheel or pip freeze, 3) server response capture (raw bytes) if possible. Can you attach?

Alice Chen: uploaded pcap to the support bucket (link: https://redwood.s3/support/pcaps/2229991234.pcap). pip freeze: redwood-sdk==0.9.4, requests==2.31.0, urllib3==1.26.16, python 3.10.11.

infra-bot: deploy to staging completed (staging: redwood/sse-tolerant-parser @ sha: a1b2c3) :white_check_mark:

Carla Gomes: I pushed a branch that accumulates raw bytes and only decodes when the decoder doesn't raise an error. Also adds explicit handling for interleaved keepalive lines that aren't prefixed with "data:". Patch: treat lines starting with "keepalive:" as no-op but do not flush decode buffer.

Ben Patel: QA: can you run the reproduction against staging build? looks like the fix will be in 0.9.7. If that passes we can ship a patch and recommend customers upgrade.

Alice Chen: ran against staging — survived 10k tokens without hang. No Unicode errors. Thanks! Workaround for users until release: set env REDWOOD_SSE_LENIENT=1 or pin to staging wheel.

Ben Patel: filing internal follow-up ticket INC-3221 for backport to 0.9.x line, and send advisory to affected customers with repro/mitigation. @Carla thanks for quick fix. :pray:

Alice Chen: adding small repro details for advisory so support can triage faster: exact symptoms: generator yields until a boundary where a multibyte token+CRLF is split across TCP frames and a keepalive line interleaves. Observed with python 3.8-3.10, requests-based transport.

SupportBot: note added to thread: escalation -> SWE until patch released.

Carla Gomes: I'll prepare patch + release notes today.

Ben Patel: great — closing escalation when patch is published and customers notified.
